name: cross-graph diamond coalesce
topology: A in g1; B,C in g2 (reached from g1 via wire bridge); D in g1. Edges A→B, A→C, B→D, C→D — a diamond split across two single-threaded graphs.
expect: DIRTY crosses the wire to B and C at the same priority as DATA (R12). Phase 1 DIRTY reaches D via both legs before any phase-2 DATA. D recomputes EXACTLY ONCE after both B and C settle in the same logical wave; D's outgoing wave contains a single DATA. No glitch (D never fires on a half-settled diamond).
note: L2.F mixed-locality survival proof — the diamond stays glitch-free even though B/C live in a different causal domain reached over the wire bridge.
blocked: wire bridge (backlog B2) — not yet implementable; the in-process diamond core it leans on is green in packages/ts core.test.ts (R-diamond/R-two-phase)

name: async-result arriving at paused node
topology: Producer P backed by an async (LocalAsync) pool → node N. N has one active pause lock.
input: 1) N.up([[PAUSE, L1]]). 2) P's async fn resolves while N is paused, delivering [[DATA, r]] toward N. 3) N.up([[RESUME, L1]]).
expect: The async result does NOT drop and does NOT deliver mid-pause; it enters N's pause buffer. On final-lock RESUME (L1 released, lockset empty) the buffered result replays as a wave to N's sinks. lock_id scope = the node-level pause_lockset (consistent with PAUSE buffering DATA).
note: DR-3 — async-result-at-paused-node is buffer+RESUME-replay, identical to how PAUSE buffers a synchronous DATA.

name: INVALIDATE × ctx.state × onInvalidate
topology: source S → derived D. D's fn sets ctx.state on each run and registers ctx.onInvalidate(flush). A second parent S2 → D exists (diamond) to exercise fan-in idempotency.
input: 1) S settles [[DATA, v]] → D runs, caches, sets ctx.state. 2) S.down([[INVALIDATE]]) — cascades to D via both fan-in paths in one wave.
expect: D broadcasts INVALIDATE downstream exactly ONCE (not once per fan-in path). D's onInvalidate hook fires exactly once (external flush). ctx.state is NOT wiped — INVALIDATE is lifecycle-continue, not a fresh-lifecycle transition; any internal reset must be done manually in onInvalidate. D's per-dep prevData returns to SENTINEL so a downstream prevData===SENTINEL never-emitted detector reads correctly. A second INVALIDATE arrival in the same wave is a no-op (hook + broadcast do not re-fire).
note: distinguishes lifecycle-continue (INVALIDATE) from fresh-lifecycle wipe (deactivation / resubscribable reset). TS arm covers single-parent cascade + idempotent no-op + state-preservation; fan-in-in-one-wave needs batch (covered by R-invalidate-idempotent _hasData guard).

name: mixed sync/async diamond
topology: A → B (sync LocalSync leg) and A → C (async LocalAsync pool leg); B→D, C→D. One diamond, one sync leg + one remote/async leg.
expect: D joins EXACTLY ONCE after BOTH legs settle, even though the async leg C settles later via a pool callback. The async pool callback's wave-state mutation serializes back onto the graph's single thread (R-graph-domain), so D's dirty-dep accounting reconciles the sync and async settlements into one recompute. The first-run gate holds D until both deps have delivered real DATA. R-dirty-before-data: a post-activation re-join emits DIRTY before DATA in the same logical wave (observed ['DIRTY','DATA'], glitch-free two-phase).
note: R8/R9 PoC validated; TS arm now a full conformance test (sync + async pool, same process — no wire bridge needed). R-dirty-before-data earned here via the post-activation re-join DIRTY-before-DATA assertion (CSP-3, 2026-05-28).

name: PAUSE lockset multi-source
topology: node N with two independent pause controllers, A and B.
input: 1) A.up([[PAUSE, LA]]). 2) B.up([[PAUSE, LB]]). 3) A.up([[PAUSE, LA]]) again (duplicate). 4) A.up([[RESUME, LA]]). 5) B.up([[RESUME, LX]]) for an unknown LX. 6) B.up([[RESUME, LB]]).
expect: After step 1-2 lockset = {LA, LB}, N paused. Step 3 (same-id repeat PAUSE) is idempotent — lockset unchanged. Step 4 removes LA; lockset = {LB}; N STILL paused (B's lock holds). Step 5 (unknown id) is a no-op. Step 6 removes LB; lockset empty; N truly resumes (fires once with latest dep values under default mode). Releasing one controller never resumes the node while another's lock is held.
note: multi-pauser correctness by construction — paused state derives from lockset.size > 0.

name: synchronous feedback cycle → ERROR
topology: state S → derived D=([S], n=>n+1) → effect E=([D]); E's fn synchronously calls S.set(...) (a write back to S, an indirect dep of E), so S→D→E plus the feedback write closes a cycle.
input: Kick the graph so E's fn runs and synchronously re-drives S (S.set) before E's wave completes.
expect: The re-entrant attempt to run E's fn while E is already mid-wave is detected node-locally (E's in-wave flag is set) and rejected: a node ON the cycle emits [[ERROR, e]] (the graph layer catches the substrate throw at the value-level wrapper nearest the throw on the synchronous unwind — D30; which node is implementation-determined, e.g. D or E), and the wave aborts deterministically. NO silent _pending desync, NO unbounded synchronous recursion / stack overflow, NO surviving half-settled state. A legitimate accumulator over the same S built with ctx.state (scan) does NOT trigger the cycle (no topological re-entry).
note: B10 / D37. Separates a disguised imperative control-flow loop (rejected) from ctx.state accumulation (allowed). Detection reuses the existing _insideRunWave flag (zero new structure); error ownership graph-level (D30); dispatcher uninvolved. Async feedback across a turn boundary (async pool) is a separate, out-of-scope case.

name: upstream control at a depless source
topology: depless source S (cached value) → derived D → sink. D (or a sink on D) originates ctx.up([msg]) which forwards upstream to the terminus S.
input: Three independent runs, one per upstream-allowed non-pause control kind: 1) D.up([[INVALIDATE]]). 2) D.up([[DIRTY]]). 3) D.up([[TEARDOWN]]).
expect: INVALIDATE: S HONORS the invalidate-request — S.cache returns to SENTINEL, S's onInvalidate hook fires once, and S broadcasts INVALIDATE downstream so D (and the whole downstream cone) clears (D.cache → SENTINEL, D's onInvalidate fires). DIRTY: DROPPED at S — S unchanged (cache + status intact), NO downstream DIRTY, downstream is NOT left wedged awaiting a settle. TEARDOWN: DROPPED at S — S not terminated, NO downstream TEARDOWN. A node guard on S may deny the INVALIDATE (drops silently) — opt-out, not the default.
note: B11 / D38. Closes the F-NO-IMPL-DEFINED gap on upstream control reaching a depless source. INVALIDATE-up is a cache-drop request (not an imperative write); DIRTY/TEARDOWN have no coherent terminus action. Dep-bearing intermediates forward only; source is the single actor, down-cascade the effect. Formal: wave_up_source.tla.

name: intra-graph runtime rewire
topology: sources A, B (B carries a cached DATA b0); derived D = ([A], fn) — D initially depends only on A. All in one graph (D22 single causal domain).
input: 1) A settles [[DATA,a1]] → D's first-run gate opens, cache=fn(a1). 2) D.addDep(B, fn2). 3) B settles [[DATA,b1]]. 4) D.removeDep(A, fn3). 5) A settles [[DATA,a2]]. 6) D.setDeps([B], fn3) (current set, idempotent). Variants: remove A while A's DIRTY is mid-flight to D; A sends [[INVALIDATE]] then D.removeDep(A); A goes terminal then attempt D.addDep(A) / attempt a rewire on a terminal D / addDep(self) / a cycle / mid-fn rewire.
expect: Surgical (Option-C): a rewire touches only changed deps — kept deps keep their subscription + DepRecord, no unsub/resub. (2) addDep(B) with B cached → B's cached value reaches D via the subscribe handshake (START then [DATA,b0] per R-push-subscribe) and D recomputes; the first-run gate is NOT re-armed (D already passed it — it does not re-wait for a fresh round of all deps); an added SENTINEL dep delivers START only, no recompute until it emits. (3) B's update drives D. (4) removeDep(A) discards A's DepRecord + clears A's dirty contribution; if A was the sole dirty contributor and D was dirty, D AUTO-SETTLES; D's cache is PRESERVED across every rewire (R-rom-ram). (5) after removeDep(A) a2 NO LONGER drives D — A's edge is DRAINED so no stale DIRTY/DATA/INVALIDATE strands. (6) setDeps to the current set is idempotent (no spurious recompute, no DepRecord churn). A mid-wave removal (A's DIRTY in flight) auto-settles per above; a removed dep's queued INVALIDATE is drained, never lands. REJECTS (throw → graph-layer ERROR, not silent): self-dependency; a cycle; setDeps/addDep/removeDep on a terminal D (completed/errored); adding a non-resubscribable terminal dep (resubscribable terminal allowed); mid-fn rewire (a fn mutating its own topology mid-wave = the D37 feedback-cycle ERROR) and reentrant rewire. removeDep to zero deps → degenerate fn-no-deps, cache preserved, no auto-deactivate. Every rewire requires an explicit fn (positional fn-deps pairing). INTRA-graph only (D22); no cross-graph rewire form.
note: D42/CSP-2.5; R-rewire (since D22, refined by D42). SUBSTRATE prerequisite for higher-order operators (mergeMap/switchMap/concatMap/exhaustMap/flatMap). Formal (SD-2 gate, all four cross-axes): wave_rewire.tla = per-node Q1–Q7 + rewire×INVALIDATE (NoStaleEdgeMessages) + rewire×terminal (RewireOnlyOnLiveNode), TLC-green 603k states; wave_rewire_emit.tla = rewire×equals (CacheMatchesLastData) + rewire×multi-sink (MultiSinkConsistent), TLC-green 3003 states; all four new invariants mutation-verified load-bearing. TS arm GREEN 2026-05-28 (setDeps/addDep/removeDep in @graphrefly/ts node.ts; conformance.test.ts C-8 + rewire.test.ts 12 unit tests); rust/py arms pending CSP-5/CSP-7. R-rewire FLIPPED ACTIVE 2026-05-28 (TS-arm-green+formal precedent).

name: pausable:false async source ignores PAUSE (keeps producing)
topology: depless async-pool source S with pausable:false (timer/interval-class) -> sink.
input: 1) subscribe a sink to S. 2) S.up([[PAUSE, L1]]). 3) S's async fn resolves, emitting [[DATA, r]] while the lock is held.
expect: DATA is delivered to the sink IMMEDIATELY (DIRTY+DATA), NOT buffered -- pausable:false ignores PAUSE/RESUME entirely; the lockset is never consulted and production continues through the PAUSE (contrast C-2, where a pausable compute node buffers). A subsequent RESUME is a no-op (nothing buffered).
note: D44 -- pausable mode is the outer gate over R-async-paused; false dominates (resolves B20).

name: true-mode async leaf source delivers own production immediately under PAUSE
topology: depless async-pool LEAF source S, pausable:true (default; fromPromise/fromAsyncIter-class) -> sink.
input: 1) subscribe a sink to S. 2) S.up([[PAUSE, L1]]). 3) S's async fn resolves, emitting [[DATA, r]] while the lock is held.
expect: DATA is delivered to the sink IMMEDIATELY (DIRTY+DATA), NOT buffered -- in true mode PAUSE gates recomputation/propagation, not a leaf source's OWN production ('production-gating is resumeAll's job'). A COMPUTE node (deps>0) in the same position WOULD buffer (C-2); with pausable:'resumeAll' the leaf source WOULD buffer.
note: D44 -- the true-mode leaf-source carve-out extends to async production (B20's twin).

name: higher-order inner rewire at the wave boundary
topology: outer source S; operator OP = ([S], fn) in one graph (D22). fn: on S DATA v -> inner = makeInner(v); ctx.rewireNext(addDep inner). on an inner COMPLETE -> ctx.rewireNext(removeDep that inner). switch-variant: on S DATA -> rewireNext(removeDep prevInner) + rewireNext(addDep newInner). Inners are leaf sources whose deactivation is observable (a flag set in onDeactivation).
input: 1) S [[DATA,v1]] -> OP requests addDep(innerA). 2) wave settles -> drain -> innerA added+subscribed, cached DATA pushed [DIRTY,DATA]. 3) innerA DATA -> forwarded. 4) (switch) S [[DATA,v2]] -> OP requests removeDep(innerA)+addDep(innerB). 5) drain -> innerA unsubscribed+drained, loses last subscriber -> _deactivate -> onDeactivation fires (cancellation observable); innerB added. 6) (merge) two inners live -> both forward. 7) an inner COMPLETEs -> removeDep -> drain removes it (bounding). Variants: IMMEDIATE in-fn this.addDep (not via rewireNext) -> REJECTED (D37); rewireNext then OP terminal same wave -> queue discarded; no-net-change rewireNext -> no-op.
expect: A rewireNext NEVER mutates _deps while _insideRunWave is true (deferred to the post-settle drain). The drain runs at the COMMITTED boundary (after batch commit / final-lock RESUME, never on an un-committed/paused view). Each queued op applied exactly once, in deterministic order (per-node FIFO, causal node order), as a fresh wave. Added cached dep pushes [DIRTY,DATA]; first-run gate NOT re-armed. Removed dep DRAINED (no stale DIRTY/DATA/INVALIDATE strands) and, if last subscriber, _deactivates + fires onDeactivation = observable input-side teardown (switchMap cancel/abortInFlight; mergeMap bounding). switch: only the current inner forwarded AND the superseded inner's source torn down (not merely masked). IMMEDIATE in-fn self-rewire still throws -> graph-layer ERROR (D37). Terminal OP discards pending queue. No-net-change rewireNext = no-op (no boundary-drain loop). INTRA-graph only.
note: D47/R-rewire-deferred; substrate prerequisite for higher-order operators. Distinct from C-8 (external/immediate rewire between waves) — C-11 is SELF-triggered/deferred-at-boundary. Formal DONE 2026-05-29: wave_rewire_deferred.tla TLC-green (5056 states, depth 23) + all 4 invariants (DeferredAppliedAtBoundary / DrainExactlyOnce / RemovedDepSilenced / NoBoundaryDrainLoop) mutation-verified load-bearing. R-rewire-deferred flips active once the C-11 TS arm is green + B15 (fn-swap handle GC) lands (SD-2). Batch/pause deferred-drain timing = backlog B24.

name: occurrences stay DATA; RESOLVED is undirty-only (no equals-substitution)
topology: (a) a source emitting a repeated value (fromIter([1,1,1])-class) -> sink. (b) the same source -> take(3) -> sink. (c) source -> filter(pred rejecting every value) -> downstream node -> sink. (d) source -> distinctUntilChanged -> sink. All intra-graph (D22).
input: (a) source emits 1,1,1 then COMPLETE. (b) same into take(3). (c) source emits values all failing the filter pred (each a dirty+settle round). (d) source emits 1,1,2.
expect: (a) the sink observes THREE DATA (1,1,1) then COMPLETE -- a repeated value is a distinct occurrence, NEVER collapsed to RESOLVED (no equals-substitution). (b) take(3) emits [1,1,1] then COMPLETE (counts occurrences, not distinct values). (c) the filter, DIRTY'd but rejecting (no tier-3 value), has the substrate SYNTHESIZE one undirty RESOLVED per wave to clear the downstream dirty -- no DATA, no wedge; RESOLVED here means dirtied-but-no-value, never value-unchanged. (d) distinctUntilChanged (opt-in dedup, its own eq) emits [1,2] -- dedup is the OPERATOR's job, not the substrate's. Every node settle is >=1 DATA XOR 1 RESOLVED, never mixed. NodeOptions.equals does not exist.
note: D49/R-resolved-undirty supersedes D15/R-equals. Pins the un-overloaded RESOLVED (undirty-only, substrate-synthesized) + no substrate dedup. Formal: wave_protocol.tla equals-substitution axis removed (+ retire wave_protocol_custom_equals_MC / wave_protocol_equals_false_MC); wave_rewire_emit.tla equals axis revised.
